source_text: Cognoscis nempe, quomodo signatissime Manichaeus traducem confirmet animarum et quo testimonio utatur ad vituperationem carnis, illo videlicet, quod in vestro ore versatur, id est: Quod nascitur de carne, caro est et, quod de spiritu, spiritus est [n212] .
pass_a_gloss: You recognize surely how most signally the Manichaean confirms a vine-layer of souls and by which testimony he uses toward the vituperation of flesh, that namely which is turned in your mouth, that is: What is born from flesh is flesh, and what from spirit is spirit.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS anima; Blaise human soul as image

pass_b_english: You surely recognize how explicitly Mani affirms the transmission of souls by descent, and which testimony he uses to condemn flesh: precisely the one constantly on your lips, ‘What is born of flesh is flesh, and what is born of spirit is spirit’ (John 3:6).

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
